newsitem.title: USA: U.S. residents said to smuggle arms from Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: U.S. residents said to smuggle arms from Vietnam.

text.p: A federal grand jury has indicted two U.S. residents on charges of conspiring to smuggle hundreds of thousands of weapons and weapon parts from Vietnam to the United States, prosecutors said on Tuesday.

The grand jury, sitting in San Francisco, charged Curtis Debord, 43, of Reno, Nev, and Peter Tran, 29, of Portland, Ore with conspiracy to smuggle firearms and firearm parts into the United States and conspiracy to deal in firearms without a license, the U.S. Attorney's office here said.

If convicted, the defendants face a maximum sentence of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine, it said in a statement. The statement did not make clear the men's whereabouts or if they had been arrested. A spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's office could not immediately be reached.

The indictment resulted from an 18-month investigation by Customs agents and agents of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms of a group of American and Vietnamese citizens, the U.S. Attorney's office said.
The targets of the probe were allegedly involved in smuggling a large volume of weapons, many of them of American origin, from Vietnam into U.S. West coast ports, it said.
Law enforcement officials in San Francisco, Sacramento, Los Angeles, San Diego and Portland, Oregon were taking part in the investigation, it said.
Two containers shipped via Hamburg, Germany containing more than 109,000 parts for light military assault weapons, were seized by U.S. Customs agents in San Diego last March.
The weapons and parts were intended for sale to firearms dealers in California and Oklahoma, among others, the U.S. Attorney's office said.
